column3: The Hebrew has a wicked person before me in the singular; BSB says the wicked are present.
The Hebrew uses an uncompleted verb for the fire burning; BSB uses burned.
The Hebrew asks to know how fleeting I am; BSB explicitly adds my life.
The Hebrew says every standing man is entirely vapor; BSB interprets standing as at his best.
The Hebrew shifts to a plural verb for making a commotion, then back to singular for heaping up; BSB uses he throughout and explicitly supplies riches.
The Hebrew has a fool in the singular; BSB has fools.
The Hebrew says because You have done it; BSB says because of what You have done.
The Hebrew describes perishing with a completed verb; BSB says I am perishing.
The Hebrew describes discipline and dissolving what he desires as completed actions; BSB uses present verbs.
The Hebrew has tear in the singular; BSB says weeping.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add again to being cheered as BSB does.
